# Results — Study 175 (Crypto-Weekend) on real BTC-USD daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Three sub-claims tested on the
BTC-USD daily tape (Yahoo Finance, 2014-09-17 to 2026-06-14): (1) weekend mean return vs
weekday, (2) weekend volatility vs weekday, (3) a weekend-only timing rule vs buy-and-hold.
Inference: Newey-West HAC t-stat with Bonferroni correction for 3 simultaneous tests
(adjusted threshold |t| ≥ 2.39 at α = 0.05/3). As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| BTC-USD | 2014-09-17 → 2026-06-14 | 4,289 | `3c26b7c8e544` |

- BTC trades 24/7 (no weekend gaps), so the weekend side has **1,226 days** (n_Sat = 613, n_Sun = 613)
  and the weekday side has **3,063 days** — far larger effective-n than most calendar anomaly studies.
- Pre-2023 sub-sample: 865 weekend days; post-2023: 361 weekend days.

## Claim 1 — mean return: weekend vs weekday

The "weekend pump" says BTC weekends are directionally distinct — either pumped or dumped by
retail-dominated order flow. On the daily open-to-close return:

| Group | n | mean (% / day) | Ann. Sharpe | HAC t vs zero |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Weekend days** | 1,226 | **+0.082%** | 0.58 | +1.09 |
| **Weekday days** | 3,063 | **+0.120%** | 0.61 | +1.55 |

- Weekend premium = weekday − weekend = **−0.038% / day** (weekends slightly *worse*, not better).
- HAC t-stat on the premium: **−0.51** — statistically indistinguishable from zero.
- Bonferroni-adjusted significance? **No** (threshold |t| ≥ 2.39). Not even naively significant.
- Pre-2023 premium: −0.047% / day, t = −0.47. Post-2023: −0.018% / day, t = −0.21.
  The "banking normalisation killed it" hypothesis has nothing to kill — the effect was never there.

## Claim 2 — volatility: weekends are *calmer*, not wilder

The folk claim says weekends are more volatile (thin liquidity, no professional market-making).
Reality is the opposite:

| Group | Ann. vol (daily) | Ratio |
|---|--:|--:|
| Weekend | **51.6%** | 0.72 |
| Weekday | **72.2%** | — |

- Weekend vol is **28% lower** than weekday vol.
- Levene HAC t-stat on the variance difference: **−9.87** — highly significant.
- The "thin-market, wild-swings" narrative is wrong: weekends are the *quiet* session.

## Claim 3 — weekend timing rule (hold weekend days, skip weekdays)

A weekend-only buy-and-hold (hold only on Saturday and Sunday daily bars) vs unconstrained B&H:

| Arm | n | gross mean (% / day) | HAC t | net (5 bps) | net t | net (10 bps) | net t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Weekend-only timing | 1,226 | +0.082% | +1.09 | −0.018% | −0.24 | −0.118% | −1.57 |

- Gross timing return: +0.082% / day, HAC t = +1.09 — positive but not significant.
- The timing rule earns *less* per day than an unconditional B&H (+0.120%), so it destroys alpha
  vs buy-and-hold even before costs.
- At 5 bps one-way (10 bps round-trip) the net is **−0.018% / day** — a dead flat line.
- No positive break-even cost exists over buy-and-hold; the rule is strictly inferior.

## Day-of-week breakdown

| Day | n | mean (% / day) | std |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Monday | 612 | **+0.416%** | 3.73% |
| Tuesday | 612 | −0.006% | 3.55% |
| Wednesday | 613 | +0.166% | 3.78% |
| Thursday | 613 | −0.103% | 4.30% |
| Friday | 613 | +0.128% | 3.45% |
| **Saturday** | 613 | +0.132% | 2.68% |
| **Sunday** | 613 | +0.033% | 2.73% |

The highest raw mean is **Monday** (+0.416%) — a well-known calendar effect in equities that
migrates into BTC. Saturday and Sunday are unremarkable and lower-volatility.

## Synthetic positive control

On a deterministic synthetic tape (``data.synthetic_daily``) with a planted weekend-boost knob,
the engine recovers the weekend premium when one exists (|t| >> 2 for boost=0.05) and reads
≈ 0 when the tape is a martingale (boost=0). The real tape's t = −0.51 is therefore a statement
about the **market**, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Weekend premium t = −0.51 (wrong sign), nowhere near the Bonferroni-adjusted
  threshold of |t| ≥ 2.39. The "weekend pump/dump" effect does not exist in the data.
- **Vol claim — MIXED/inverted.** Weekends are significantly *calmer* (Levene t = −9.87, ratio 0.72),
  the opposite of the folk story. This is genuine but not a tradable edge.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The timing rule is inferior to buy-and-hold before costs; costs push it
  firmly negative. A hold-weekends-only strategy captures only 29% of calendar days while earning
  less per day, compounding into a large opportunity cost.
- **3rd axis — Vol claim: Inverted.** Weekends are the *quiet* session, significantly less volatile.
  The "thin-liquidity, wild-weekends" narrative is exactly backwards.
